subject: Schema crosswalk & implementation guide for streaming + tool calls
messages:
From: Claire Park <claire.park@medisynchealth.com>

Cc: integration@medisynchealth.com

Subject: Schema crosswalk & implementation guide for streaming + tool calls

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re ready to move into technical onboarding and want a concise crosswalk between our existing event schema and Redwood’s structured-output schema, plus a short implementation guide for: streaming outputs, function/tool calling (we plan to call a medication-lookup service), and the JSON schemas you expect for structured outputs.

What we need from Redwood:
- A mapping document that aligns our event payload fields to Redwood’s structured-output fields (preferably an Excel crosswalk we can import)
- Examples of streaming responses and how KV/prefix caching will affect reconnections
- An example function/tool calling contract (input/output JSON and error cases) for our medication-lookup endpoint
- Recommended rollout plan (canary + validation steps) and a checklist of required logs/artifacts for our security/compliance team

We can provide our current event schema (attached) and a 2-week implementation window starting Apr 26. Can we set a 60m technical working session next week (Apr 20–22)? Prefer AM PT.

Attached: current_event_schema_v3.json (exported)

Best,
Claire
Senior Product Manager — Integrations
MediSync Health

Claire —

Appreciate the clear ask and the schema file. Monica (solutions engineer) and Camila (CS lead) are looped in — we’ll own the crosswalk and the guide. High-level plan from our side:

1) Pre-work (by Apr 22): we review your schema and create an initial crosswalk (Excel) and a short JSON schema for the structured output you’ll receive.
2) Technical working session (60m) — propose Apr 21 at 09:30 AM PT. Monica will run the session and capture live decisions.
3) Implementation week (Apr 26–May 7): we’ll provide sample code snippets for streaming with reconnect semantics, a function-call contract for medication-lookup, and a canary rollout checklist.

What we need from you before the session:
- Typical event rates (p50/p95) and expected peak concurrency (tokens/sec or requests/sec)
- A short list of required fields that must be preserved end-to-end for your downstream systems
- Any compliance constraints (data retention/hashing) you require in the wire format

I’m attaching our onboarding checklist for the session. If 09:30 AM PT on Apr 21 works, we’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Attachment: rishi_onboarding_checklist.pdf

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Park <claire.park@medisynchealth.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: camila.reyes@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-19T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Schema crosswalk & implementation guide for streaming + tool calls

Claire, Rishi —

Thanks for the file, Claire. I dug into current_event_schema_v3.json and sketched an initial mapping and implementation notes — attached as schema_crosswalk_v1.xlsx. Highlights here so the working session can focus on decisions, not discovery: 

- Streaming expectations:
  - We recommend a server-sent events (SSE) or HTTP/2 streaming path for low-latency token delivery. If you must use websockets, we’ll provide the same structured payloads but the reconnect semantics differ slightly.
  - KV/prefix cache: prefix caching will help for repeated prompts (e.g., patient context). On reconnect, the client should supply a short session fingerprint to allow server-side KV reuse; we include a small snippet in the crosswalk.

- Structured outputs:
  - We propose an output envelope: {"schema_version","response_type","structured_payload":{"diagnoses":[],"medications":[],"confidenceScores":{}}} — see JSON examples in the spreadsheet.
  - Required preservation: patient_id, encounter_id, timestamp. These must be passed back in the structured_payload metadata field to satisfy your downstream join keys.

- Tool calling (medication-lookup):
  - Contract (high level): input {"patient_id","query_med_name","context_tokens"} -> output {"matches":[{"drug_id","rxnorm_id","dosage_suggestions"}],"errors":[]}
  - Error handling: define clear error codes for ambiguous matches vs external API failures; Redwood’s function-calling layer will surface these in the response envelope so your logic can retry or surface to clinicians.

I also attached a short checklist of logs we’ll surface for compliance (request_id, model_version, token_counts, routing_decision).

See attached spreadsheets and let me know if you want a pre-read call; otherwise I’ll run the Apr 21 session at 09:30 AM PT and walk through the crosswalk live.

—Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: schema_crosswalk_v1.xlsx

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Park <claire.park@medisynchealth.com>, monica.patel@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-20T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Schema crosswalk & implementation guide for streaming + tool calls

Claire —

Great to be working together. A few implementation-level items I want on the record so the kickoff is efficient:

- Canary rollout plan (recommended):
  1) Internal integration tests against a staging medication-lookup (0% user traffic) — 2 days
  2) Canary (1% user traffic with active monitoring of structured-output diffs + accuracy) — 3 days
  3) Ramp to 20% with checkpoints (latency SLO, error rate, false-positive medication matches) — 5 days
  4) Full production with ongoing quality monitoring and rollback tags

- Validation steps:
  - Use the sample prompt set (we’ll provide 200 cases) and run a structured-output diff against your current baseline; we’ll provide a small eval harness to automate this.
  - Schema enforcement: Redwood can validate incoming structured_payload against the JSON schema and reject/flag non-conformant messages with a validation code.

- Observability + artifacts for your security team:
  - We’ll share token-level cost breakdowns per call for the canary, request/response logs (redacted per your policy), and model_version tags.

Proposed deliverables post-session (attached as implementation_timeline.xlsx): initial crosswalk, function-call contract, sample streaming client snippet (node/python), and canary checklist.

Best,
Camila
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: implementation_timeline.xlsx
